Welcome! I’m so glad you’re here to join this journey with me.
Imagine a landscape shaped not just by rivers and mountains, but by the stories, memories, and myths that flow through the heart of North America.
As we travel together, we’ll explore the tangled relationship between Indigenous peoples and the societies that have grown up around them—where history, memory, and myth collide, creating a complex web that still shapes our world today.
Now, if you’re curious about how these stories get told, and even more curious about the truths that sometimes get lost along the way, you’re in the right place. Because that’s exactly what Thomas King invites us to do in his thought-provoking book, The Inconvenient Indian: A Curious Account of Native People in North America.
With his signature blend of wit, honesty, and sharp insight, King doesn’t just recount the past—he brings it right into the present, asking us to look again at the stories we think we know.
We’ll meet familiar figures and revisit pivotal moments, but we’ll also see how tales have been twisted, retold, or sometimes just plain ignored to suit certain interests.
Through these pages, we’ll discover the enduring strength of Native communities—their resilience, their ongoing struggle for recognition and justice, and the powerful ways they use storytelling to survive and resist.
So, as we set out, let’s keep our minds open and our curiosity alive. Together, we’ll challenge old assumptions, uncover hidden truths, and hopefully, come away with a deeper understanding of the questions and voices that continue to shape this continent.
Ready to dive in? Let’s explore what lies beneath the surface—together.
